headline: High risk of filesystem conflict and cascading miscoordination; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads files passed on the command line and writes diffs, while pipecat can carry text through a shared bus and multiple transports. No direct shared channel is documented, so only manual copy/paste or explicit file handoff creates an injection path. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF an operator copies pipecat-generated text into files Mentat reads, THEN prompt injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared message bus or clipboard bridge, THEN attacker-controlled text can cross between them.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any manual copy/paste bridge for untrusted text.
Require human review before Mentat applies diffs.
Use a provenance tag on any text handed from pipecat to Mentat.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction-stripping at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys; pipecat commonly sends audio, text, and conversation state to external STT/LLM/TTS services. If they share a workspace or hand off files, source code or secrets can flow into pipecat-connected third parties. The interaction is not fully documented, so uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF Mentat files or secrets are placed into pipecat inputs, THEN those contents can be transmitted to external services.
IF both agents operate on the same shared workspace, THEN source code can be exposed through pipecat's API-backed services.
mitigations: Do not route source files through pipecat services.
Separate secrets from any shared workspace.
Use local-only models for any text that originated in Mentat.
Review outbound destinations in pipecat before enabling it.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention at the integration boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem. Pipecat supports shared-bus concurrency across processes and machines. If both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking, creating destructive conflicts by default in shared deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, THEN file clobbering or inconsistent edits can occur.
IF pipecat and Mentat both mutate git state without a lock, THEN commits or diffs can conflict.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize all writes with a lock file.
Disable git mutation in one agent during shared runs.
Run a pre-commit diff check before applying changes.
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and pipecat can move text through conversational pipelines and downstream services. If pipecat treats Mentat output as authoritative, errors can cascade into spoken, logged, or acted-upon outputs. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, so the risk is real but not necessarily irreversible.
conditions: IF pipecat forwards Mentat's proposed edits without verification, THEN incorrect code can propagate downstream.
IF Mentat's diffs are rendered or spoken by pipecat as final, THEN a single error can cascade across outputs.
mitigations: Require a verification step before pipecat relays Mentat output.
Show Mentat diffs as suggestions, not facts.
Add a checksum or diff review gate.
Log provenance for every forwarded edit.
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat handles source code and model-provider API keys, while pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state and can call many third-party APIs. If regulated or sensitive content is routed through pipecat services, retention or residency mismatches can arise. The profiles do not document a shared compliance regime, so the safer severity is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent from Mentat into pipecat's external services, THEN residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF the deployment requires strict deletion/export handling, THEN pipecat's third-party service chain may not satisfy it.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of pipecat integrations.
Review retention settings for every external service.
Document the data flow from Mentat to pipecat.
Use a local-only deployment for sensitive workloads.
requires-engineering: obtain and enforce a DPA or equivalent controls.
